result.note: Tested the national non-fossil targets and storage VGF support, plus the location of the 7 GWh battery project; the Rajasthan coal projection and the permit review are projections, so they were skipped.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's power sector, as reported in January 2026:
items: India is targeting 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.
The government says non-fossil sources crossed 50% of India's installed power capacity in June 2025.
Viability Gap Funding support for battery storage covers up to 60% of capital expenditure.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because Viability Gap Funding for storage covers up to 40% of capex, not 60%. Even with the 500 GW target and the 50% milestone, coal remains central in the interim because wind and solar cannot yet guarantee round-the-clock supply.
questions.source: New Delhi is still targeting 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030 and says non-fossil sources crossed 50% of installed capacity in June 2025.

questions.prompt: In January 2026, GoodEnough Energy announced the commissioning of a 7 GWh battery storage system, which it claimed was India's largest. In which state is it located?
questions.explain: GoodEnough Energy commissioned the 7 GWh system in Uttar Pradesh. The story presents it as a sign that batteries are moving from a niche add-on to the backbone of the grid, as renewables struggle to meet peak-hour demand.
questions.source: A day later, GoodEnough Energy announced that it had commissioned a 7 GWh battery storage system in Uttar Pradesh, claiming it to be India’s largest.
